title: UNIT 4: GENETICS
notes:
✓ Genetics is the study of heredity and variation.

→ It explains how traits are passed from parents to offspring through genetic material.

title: 4.1 THE GENETIC MATERIALS
notes:
✓ Genetic material carries hereditary information. DNA is the main genetic material; RNA acts as genetic material in some viruses.

◆ Gene → unit of heredity.
◆ Chromosome → DNA-protein structure carrying genes.
◆ Allele → alternative form of a gene.
◆ Genome → complete genetic material.

title: 4.2 STRUCTURE & FUNCTION OF DNA AND RNA
notes:
✓ Both DNA and RNA are nucleic acids made of nucleotides.

◆ DNA → double-stranded, deoxyribose, bases A-T-G-C → stores genetic information.

◆ RNA → usually single-stranded, ribose, bases A-U-G-C → mainly helps protein synthesis.

title: 4.2.1 STRUCTURE & FUNCTION OF DNA
notes:
✓ DNA forms a double helix with sugar-phosphate backbones and complementary bases.

◆ A pairs with T.
◆ G pairs with C.
◆ Stores hereditary information.
◆ Controls protein production.
◆ Replicates before cell division.

title: 4.2.3 DNA REPLICATION
notes:
✓ DNA replication produces two identical DNA molecules.

→ DNA unwinds.
→ Strands separate.
→ Complementary nucleotides attach.
→ Two DNA molecules form.

◆ Semi-conservative → each new DNA has one old and one new strand.

title: 4.2.2 STRUCTURE & FUNCTION OF RNA
notes:
✓ RNA is usually single-stranded and contains ribose and A, U, G, C bases.

◆ mRNA → carries genetic message.
◆ tRNA → carries amino acids.
◆ rRNA → forms part of ribosomes and helps protein synthesis.

title: 4.3 THE PROCESS OF CELL DIVISION
notes:
✓ Cell division produces new cells for growth, repair and reproduction.

◆ Mitosis → 2 identical diploid cells.
◆ Meiosis → 4 genetically different haploid cells.

→ Meiosis creates variation through crossing over and independent assortment.

title: 4.3.1 CELL DIVISION
notes:
✓ Mitosis: Prophase → Metaphase → Anaphase → Telophase → Cytokinesis.

◆ Meiosis I → separates homologous chromosomes.
◆ Meiosis II → separates sister chromatids.

→ Crossing over occurs during Prophase I.

title: 4.4 PROTEIN SYNTHESIS
notes:
✓ Protein synthesis occurs through two stages:

◆ Transcription → DNA → mRNA.
◆ Translation → mRNA → protein.

→ mRNA carries the message, tRNA brings amino acids, and ribosomes join amino acids into proteins.

title: 4.5 MENDELIAN INHERITANCE
notes:
✓ Mendelian inheritance explains transmission of traits controlled by individual genes.

◆ Dominant allele → expressed when present.
◆ Recessive allele → expressed when no dominant allele is present.
◆ Genotype → genetic makeup.
◆ Phenotype → observable trait.

title: 4.5.1 MENDELIAN CROSSES
notes:
✓ Punnett squares predict offspring genotypes and phenotypes.

◆ Law of segregation → allele pairs separate during gamete formation.
◆ Independent assortment → alleles of different genes can be inherited independently.

title: 4.5.2 MONOHYBRID CROSS
notes:
✓ A monohybrid cross follows one trait.

AA × aa → F₁: all Aa

Aa × Aa → F₂:
◆ Genotype = 1:2:1.
◆ Phenotype = 3:1.

title: 4.5.3 DIHYBRID CROSS
notes:
✓ A dihybrid cross follows two traits simultaneously.

→ When genes assort independently, the F₂ phenotypic ratio is:

◆ 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.

title: 4.5.4 TEST CROSSES
notes:
✓ A test cross determines an unknown dominant genotype by crossing it with a homozygous recessive individual.

◆ AA × aa → all dominant.
◆ Aa × aa → 1 dominant : 1 recessive.

title: 4.6 SEX DETERMINATION
notes:
✓ Human sex is determined by X and Y chromosomes.

◆ Female = XX.
◆ Male = XY.

→ Egg always carries X; sperm carries X or Y. Therefore, sperm determines the sex of the offspring.

title: 4.7 NON-MENDELIAN INHERITANCE
notes:
✓ Inheritance patterns that do not follow simple complete dominance include:

◆ Codominance.
◆ Incomplete dominance.
◆ Multiple alleles.
◆ Rh inheritance.
◆ Sex-linked inheritance.
◆ Environmental effects.

title: 4.7.1 CODOMINANCE, INCOMPLETE DOMINANCE & MULTIPLE ALLELES
notes:
◆ Codominance → both alleles fully expressed; example: AB blood group.
◆ Incomplete dominance → intermediate phenotype; example: red × white → pink.
◆ Multiple alleles → more than two alleles exist in a population; example: ABO blood group.

title: 4.7.2 Rh FACTOR INHERITANCE
notes:
✓ Rh-positive blood has the Rh antigen; Rh-negative blood lacks it.

→ Rh incompatibility can occur when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive fetus and may cause problems in later pregnancies.

title: 4.7.3 SEX-LINKED INHERITANCE
notes:
✓ Sex-linked traits are controlled by genes on sex chromosomes, especially the X chromosome.

◆ X-linked recessive traits are more common in males.
◆ Examples → hemophilia and color blindness.

title: 4.7.4 ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS ON PHENOTYPE
notes:
✓ Phenotype = genotype + environmental influence.

◆ Temperature, nutrition, chemicals and other environmental factors can affect traits.

◆ Phenocopy → environmentally produced phenotype resembling a genetically controlled trait.

title: 4.8 HUMAN PEDIGREE ANALYSIS
notes:
✓ A pedigree traces inheritance of traits through generations.

◆ □ Male.
◆ ○ Female.
◆ ■/● Affected.

→ Horizontal line → parents.
→ Vertical line → offspring.

✓ Helps identify inheritance patterns and predict genetic risks.

title: 4.9 GENETIC DISORDERS
notes:
✓ Genetic disorders result from changes or mutations in DNA.

◆ Single-gene disorders.
◆ Chromosomal disorders.
◆ Multifactorial disorders.

◆ Examples → hemophilia, cystic fibrosis, albinism, Down syndrome and Turner syndrome.

title: 4.9.1 SINGLE-GENE DISORDERS
notes:
✓ Caused by mutation in one gene.

◆ Autosomal dominant → Huntington's disease.
◆ Autosomal recessive → cystic fibrosis, albinism.
◆ X-linked → hemophilia, color blindness.

title: 4.9.2 CHROMOSOMAL DISORDERS
notes:
✓ Caused by abnormal chromosome number or structure.

◆ Aneuploidy → abnormal chromosome number.
◆ Deletion → chromosome segment lost.
◆ Inversion → segment reversed.
◆ Translocation → segment moves to another chromosome/location.

→ Down syndrome = Trisomy 21.

title: 4.9.3 MULTIFACTORIAL DISORDERS
notes:
✓ Result from interactions between several genes and environmental factors.

◆ Examples → diabetes and many forms of cancer.

◆ Risk factors may include diet, smoking, alcohol use, lifestyle and environmental exposure.

title: 4.10 GENETIC TESTING & COUNSELING
notes:
✓ Genetic testing → identifies genetic changes and disease risks.
◆ Genetic counseling → explains genetic risks and helps families make informed decisions.

→ Used in diagnosis, risk assessment and family planning.

title: 4.11 GENE THERAPY
notes:
✓ Gene therapy modifies genetic material to treat disease.

◆ Replace a defective gene.
◆ Inactivate a harmful gene.
◆ Introduce a useful gene.
◆ Edit mutated genes.

✓ Challenges → delivery, immune response, unintended effects and cost.

title: 4.12 BREEDING
notes:
✓ Breeding uses genetic principles to improve desirable traits in plants and animals.

◆ Selective breeding → humans choose desired parents.
◆ Inbreeding → breeding closely related organisms.
◆ Crossbreeding → breeding different varieties or breeds.

→ Goal → improve useful characteristics.

title: 4.13 BIOINFORMATICS
notes:
✓ Bioinformatics combines biology + computer science + information technology to analyze biological data.

◆ Genomics → DNA/genome analysis.
◆ Proteomics → protein study.
◆ Systems biology → interactions among biological components.

→ Uses → disease diagnosis, vaccine development, genome analysis and evolutionary studies.
